project.name: AI_Research_Agent
project.description: Kiln is an evidence-backed decision research system for applied AI and LLM engineering, covering serving, RAG, agents, evaluation, and fine-tune versus retrieval tradeoffs. It pairs a LangGraph research agent with a NestJS job API, a React dashboard, and a curated docs corpus. Note: this project has over 100 source files; consider scoping analysis to a subdirectory for faster results.

nodes.name: 001_research_lifecycle_owner.sql
nodes.summary: First Postgres migration that gives research runs an execution-ownership lifecycle: it adds execution/version, job, timing and heartbeat columns to research_runs, adds execution/attempt/sequence ordering columns to run_events, and introduces the research_dispatch_outbox table for transactional job dispatch.
nodes.languageNotes: Wrapped in BEGIN/COMMIT and written entirely with IF NOT EXISTS guards, so the migration is idempotent and safe to re-run by the compose migrate service.

nodes.name: research_dispatch_outbox
nodes.summary: Transactional outbox table holding pending research job dispatches, keyed to a run and its execution version, with payload, attempt counter and dispatched_at marker plus a partial index over undispatched rows.
nodes.languageNotes: The partial index on (created_at, id) WHERE dispatched_at IS NULL keeps the pending-work scan cheap as dispatched history grows.

nodes.name: 002_knowledge_corpus.sql
nodes.summary: Second Postgres migration that provisions the reusable knowledge and corpus layer: it creates knowledge_records for cached cited answers, corpus_documents for chunked and embedded evidence, and corpus_sync_runs for tracking indexing generations, then backfills extra columns and indexes on each.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a create-then-ALTER ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS style so the same file can both initialise a fresh database and incrementally upgrade one created by an earlier schema version.

nodes.name: knowledge_records
nodes.summary: Stores reusable research answers with their citations, embedding and embedding model, plus fingerprint/query arrays, depth score, reuse counters and status used to decide when a past run can be replayed instead of re-researched.

nodes.name: corpus_documents
nodes.summary: Holds retrievable evidence chunks with source url, host, tier, quote and credibility score, plus source_path/chunk_index provenance and generation/active flags that support atomic corpus re-indexing.
nodes.languageNotes: The unique index on (source_path, chunk_index) makes re-ingesting a corpus file an upsert rather than a duplicate insert.

nodes.name: corpus_sync_runs
nodes.summary: Audit table recording each corpus indexing run with its status, generation number, source hash, document counts, embedding model and error text, so partially failed syncs can be detected and retried.

nodes.name: 02_agent_loops_vs_pipelines.md

nodes.name: 05_finetune_vs_rag_vs_context.md
nodes.summary: Corpus evidence note comparing fine-tuning, RAG, and long context for injecting new facts, recommending RAG for volatile facts, light SFT/DPO for format, and long context for retrieved packs.

nodes.name: 06_tool_calling_reliability.md
nodes.summary: Corpus evidence note on tool-calling reliability, explaining that constrained decoding fixes format but not tool or argument choice, and that retries, schema validation, and idempotent tools matter more than model swaps.

nodes.name: 07_observability_cost.md
nodes.summary: Corpus evidence note on per-node tracing and cost attribution for research agents, covering token accounting, planner/critic/report cost splits, and the need for durable run events to debug loops and HITL.

nodes.name: 08_benchmark_caveats.md

nodes.name: 09_multiagent_myths.md

nodes.name: 10_prompt_injection.md

nodes.name: 11_quantization_quality.md

nodes.name: 12_embeddings_rerank.md

tour.title: Kiln Project Overview
tour.description: Begin with the README to understand Kiln's purpose: evidence-backed decision research for applied AI and LLM engineering. It introduces the Research, Scenarios, Corpus, and Workspace surfaces, sketches the LangGraph loop, and maps the Python agent, NestJS API, React UI, and data services that the rest of the tour follows.

tour.title: Job API Entry
tour.description: The NestJS entry point starts the public-facing job API, while the root and research modules establish validation, authentication, queueing, persistence, and feature wiring. After the README's system map, these files show how external requests first enter Kiln and are routed toward the research lifecycle.
tour.languageLesson: NestJS uses decorators and module metadata to assemble controllers and providers through dependency injection; TypeScript decorator metadata must remain enabled for this runtime wiring.

tour.title: Agent Service Entry
tour.description: The FastAPI entry point exposes execution, resume, corpus, knowledge, and scenario endpoints consumed by the Job API. Its runtime owns LangGraph compilation, checkpoint readiness, streaming execution, and resume behavior, revealing the boundary between HTTP transport and the durable research engine.
tour.languageLesson: FastAPI derives request handling and validation from Python type annotations and Pydantic models, while async generators are a natural fit for streaming incremental execution frames.

tour.title: Contracts and State
tour.description: With both service entries established, study the contracts and state models that let them communicate consistently. Zod validates cross-application payloads, Pydantic defines the research vocabulary, and ResearchState carries plans, evidence, budgets, and results through the graph.
tour.languageLesson: Zod and Pydantic turn runtime validation schemas into typed application boundaries, preventing untrusted JSON from being treated as valid domain state merely because it matches a compile-time type.

tour.title: Research Graph Loop
tour.description: The graph builder assembles Kiln's core research loop and conditionally routes work through briefing, planning, evidence collection, criticism, and reporting. The critic can send insufficient work back for follow-up, while the HITL node can pause execution for an operator, making this a durable agent loop rather than a linear pipeline.

tour.title: Evidence Retrieval Pipeline
tour.description: The planner's questions become evidence through local corpus loading, chunking, embedding, hybrid ranking, and Qdrant-backed storage. These components combine lexical and semantic signals instead of assuming dense vectors alone are sufficient, and the docs graph node feeds the ranked evidence back into the workflow from Step 5.

tour.title: Grounded Report Assembly
tour.description: Once evidence is collected, coverage rules identify unanswered dimensions, citation logic binds claims to sources, and grounding checks weaken or caveat unsupported assertions. Report composition then turns that verified material into decision-oriented memos, preserving Kiln's central promise that conclusions remain traceable to evidence.

tour.title: Durable Job Lifecycle
tour.description: Return to the Job API to follow a run from controller to service, transactional repository, outbox dispatcher, and BullMQ worker. This design separates accepting a request from executing it, while persisted execution frames and fenced ownership make retries, crashes, SSE replay, and agent resumes manageable.

tour.title: Persistent Data Model
tour.description: The Postgres schema makes the durable lifecycle from Step 8 concrete through research runs, append-only events, and a transactional dispatch outbox. The knowledge and corpus tables separately preserve reusable cited answers and generation-aware evidence chunks, tying operational reliability to the retrieval and memory systems.
tour.languageLesson: A transactional outbox writes domain state and a pending message in the same database transaction, then publishes asynchronously; this avoids losing queue work between a successful commit and a process crash.

tour.title: User Experience Flow
tour.description: The React entry and root component expose the four product surfaces introduced in Step 1, with the Research page visualizing streamed graph progress, evidence, citations, and HITL decisions. The typed API wrapper validates backend responses against shared contracts, carrying the service guarantees from Step 4 all the way to the browser.
tour.languageLesson: React components compose the UI from state and hooks, while runtime Zod parsing at the fetch boundary protects the component tree from malformed server responses.

tour.title: Corpus and Evaluation
tour.description: Kiln's evidence quality begins with curated corpus notes and is guarded by a domain golden set that specifies expected routing, source tiers, forbidden claims, and contradiction handling. The offline evaluation runner turns those expectations into a regression gate, checking routing and citation quality rather than relying only on generic LLM benchmarks.

tour.title: Full Stack Deployment
tour.description: Docker Compose assembles Postgres, Redis, Qdrant, the agent, migrations, API, and web UI with health checks and persistent volumes. The environment template and service images show how the architecture's configuration, secrets, build artifacts, and startup dependencies are translated into a runnable system.
tour.languageLesson: Compose health checks and dependency conditions express readiness ordering, while named volumes preserve database, vector, and agent state independently of replaceable containers.

tour.title: Developer Quality Gates
tour.description: Finish with the developer task runner and CI workflow that operationalize the previous steps. Local targets cover service startup, corpus seeding, tests, and evaluation, while parallel CI jobs build and type-check both TypeScript applications and run the Python test and routing suites.
tour.languageLesson: GitHub Actions jobs run independently for parallel feedback, while steps within each job run sequentially; explicit language versions keep local and CI behavior aligned.
